title: A 3D Cell Culture Model Identifies Wnt/β‐Catenin Mediated Inhibition of p53 as a Critical Step during Human Hepatocyte Regeneration

evidence_spans.quote: Here, a 3D spheroid model of PHH is established
primary human hepatocytes (PHH)
its proliferative senescence-inducing target PAI1
integrative time-lapse multi-omics analyses

scope_reviewer.uncertainty_reason: The abstract uses a senescence-related modifier without showing that a senescent state is measured or analyzed, and names multi-omics without specifying molecular layers.
scope_reviewer.concise_rationale: This is a primary human-hepatocyte regeneration study. Aging relevance is unresolved because senescence is only invoked as a modifier of PAI1, and the generic multi-omics label does not identify countable layers.

causal_design_reviewer.exposure_or_intervention: Activation of Wnt signaling through external cues
causal_design_reviewer.comparator: External cues alone versus no stated activation condition
causal_design_reviewer.outcome: p53 and PAI1 (SERPINE1) inhibition and primary human hepatocyte proliferation
causal_design_reviewer.estimand_or_contrast: Wnt activation was sufficient to inhibit p53/PAI1 and drive proliferation of >50% of PHH.

adjudication.uncertainty_reason: The abstract does not establish that cellular senescence or another aging construct is measured or analyzed, and it does not name the molecular layers used in the stated multi-omics analysis.
adjudication.concise_rationale: This is an empirical primary study of human hepatocyte regeneration. Senescence is only a modifier of a target, so aging relevance remains unresolved; the reported Wnt perturbation therefore does not identify an effect on an eligible aging construct at title/abstract stage.
